hints: Write the wind as $p\ihat  + q\jhat $. Each observation tells you the direction of (wind − woman’s velocity). Which component does each observation fix?
worded:
1. Let the wind be p î + q ĵ. Walking north at 10, the apparent wind is p î + (q − 10) ĵ.

2. It seems to come from the west, i.e. it blows purely towards the east: q − 10 = 0, so q = 10, and p > 0.

3. At 30 km/h north, the apparent wind is p î + (10 − 30) ĵ = p î − 20 ĵ.

4. From the north-west means blowing towards the south-east, equal east and south parts: p = 20.

5. So the wind is 20 î + 10 ĵ km/h. (A)
conventional:
![](asset:P000262-sol-1)

Let $\vec{v}_{w} = p\ihat  + q\jhat $.

(i) $\vec{v}_{w} - 10\jhat  = p\ihat  + (q - 10)\jhat $ points east $\Rightarrow q = 10$.

(ii) $\vec{v}_{w} - 30\jhat  = p\ihat  - 20\jhat $ points south-east $\Rightarrow p = 20$.

$$\vec{v}_{w} = 20\ihat  + 10\jhat \ km/h.$$
mistakes: “From the west” is the direction the wind comes from; it blows towards the east.
The apparent wind is wind minus observer, not wind plus observer.
